text.p: Austro-Italian insurer EA-Generali said on Thursday it would lead a consortium that will make an offer for privatisation candidate Creditanstalt on Friday, when the latest tender for the bank closes.
In a statement, it said the consortium of bidders included Germany's Commerzbank, Banca Commerciale Italiana and Belgium's Bacob, the country's seventh-largest bank.
EA-Generali said it would bid for a "substantial part" of the government's 70 percent voting stake in Creditanstalt, Austria's second-biggest bank. No further details were available.

EA-Generali, majority-controlled by Italy's Assicurazioni Generali, added it welcomed the return of savings bank Die Erste into the consortium. Die Erste on Wednesday said it had rejoined the group after leaving it on September 6 following disagreement over a joint bid.

The consortium, which first made an offer for parts of the state's stake in September but was turned down by Finance Minister Viktor Klima, also included several Austrian industrial interests, ranging from electronics to beverages.

Austrian media earlier this week reported the group was likely to bid around 10 billion schillings ($944.9 million) for a large part of the government's stake, which is worth about 14.5 billion schillings at current market prices.

In September, the consortium bid some 6.7 billion schillings for roughly half the state's 19.9 million voting shares in the bank, but was rejected by Klima who said he wanted to sell the stake in its entirety.

Klima recently hinted he would be more flexible in the latest tender, widely seen as the government's last chance to close what has become Austria's longest running privatisation project since World War Two.

The government has been trying to unload its stake in Creditanstalt for more than six years now. Sources close to the Finance Ministry said around five interested parties had asked for an information memorandum on the bank on which they could base a potential bid. -- Knut Engelmann, Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274 ($ = 10.58 Austrian Schillings)
